articles.title: ChatGPT plugins
GPTs are GPTs: An early look at the labor market impact potential of large language models

articles.author: Nicola Jones
articles.description: In a year of funding chaos, ongoing climate change and pollution perils, we also saw the most powerful telescope yet, personalized gene therapy, and the next-best-thing to an HIV vaccine — not to mention a brand-new color
articles.title: Top science stories of 2025

articles.author: Carolyn Wilke
articles.description: A push to move away from petroleum products — plus the perception that natural is gentler — has scientists lathering up new ingredients, from wood and fungus extracts to engineered proteins
articles.title: The science of green hair care

articles.author: Elie Dolgin
articles.description: In polar bears, dolphins, baboons and more, molecular signatures of aging are changing how conservationists assess population health, resilience and risk
articles.title: The clock is ticking: How epigenetics could help save wildlife from collapse

articles.author: Michele Cohen Marill
articles.description: Scientists are learning more about this leading complication of childbirth. Treatments are improving and doctors can test for biological markers that flag heightened risk.
articles.title: Postpartum depression: Better remedies, and now a predictive blood test

articles.author: Richard Stone
articles.description: Doctors and scientists are waging a shadow war in the besieged nation: bacteria that are resistant to multiple antibiotics. The deadly bugs are now knocking on western Europe’s door.
articles.title: The pernicious infections infiltrating Ukraine’s front lines

articles.author: M. Mitchell Waldrop
articles.description: Superionic materials have spawned hope for a new generation of power packs for electric cars, with a promise of greater range, faster charges and more safety. But scaling up won’t be easy.
articles.title: Will your next EV have a solid-state battery — and improved performance?

articles.author: Katarina Zimmer
articles.description: Early in evolution, we animals lost the ability to manufacture nine of the 20 building blocks needed to make proteins. Herbivores evolved an impressive array of tricks to ensure their dietary needs are met.
articles.title: How plant-eaters snag their essential amino acids

articles.author: Lela Nargi
articles.description: A new technique for detecting unknown and unlooked-for chemicals is revealing dozens of contaminants in alligators, sea lions and condors
articles.title: Tracking down the hidden pollutants that make wildlife sick

articles.author: Andrew Singer
articles.description: Handled right, AI has potential to bring back middle-skill jobs lost to the rise of computers, economists argue. Or, like the mechanized mills of the past, it could toss whole sectors out of work.
articles.title: What happens to the weavers? Lessons for AI from the Industrial Revolution

articles.description: Addressing poverty helps to curb thefts and burglaries, but offenses like assaults and shootings need more innovative approaches

articles.description: Machine learning is expanding scientists’ catalogs of quakes and refining maps of underground faults. It also promises to improve quake forecasts.

articles.description: For this chore, the human touch still beats machines. But maybe not for long.
